title: Open-subscheme Ext transport compatible with scalar maps and base change
statement: Let $R,S$ be commutative rings in the same universe, $S$ an $R$-algebra, $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ a scheme morphism, $M$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module, and $j:W\hookrightarrow X$ an arbitrary open subscheme. Use the base-change schemes, module pullbacks, underlying abelian sheaves, scalar representations and adjoint coefficient morphisms of [def-pc-flat-cohomology-comparison]. Put $p:X_S\to X$, $p_W:W_S\to W$, $M_W=j^*M$, $F=U(M)$, $F_W=U(M_W)$, $N=U(p^*M)$ and $N_W=U(p_W^*M_W)$. Let $G=p^{-1}$ and $G_W=p_W^{-1}$ on abelian sheaves, and let $\varphi:G F\to N$ and $\varphi_W:G_W F_W\to N_W$ be the adjoints of the module pullback units. Write $\rho,\rho_W$ for the $R$-scalar representations on $F,F_W$, and $\tau,\tau_W$ for the $S$-scalar representations on $N,N_W$, induced by the displayed scheme morphisms to the affine bases. Write $L_W$ for the free abelian sheaf represented by $W$ in $X$, and $L_{\top,W}$ for the free sheaf represented by the top open of the scheme $W$ [lem-pc-free-mayer-vietoris-short-exact]. For all $n\geq0$ there exist additive equivalences $t_n:\operatorname{Ext}^n_W(L_{\top,W},F_W)\cong\operatorname{Ext}^n_X(L_W,F)$ and $t_n':\operatorname{Ext}^n_{W_S}(G_W L_{\top,W},N_W)\cong\operatorname{Ext}^n_{X_S}(G L_W,N)$ such that, writing $x\cdot\alpha$ for Ext postcomposition with the degree-zero class of $\alpha$, $t_n(x\cdot\rho_W(a))=t_n(x)\cdot\rho(a)$ for $a\in R$, $t_n'(y\cdot\tau_W(b))=t_n'(y)\cdot\tau(b)$ for $b\in S$, and $t_n'(G_W(x)\cdot\varphi_W)=G(t_n(x))\cdot\varphi$. No flatness, finiteness, nonemptiness or quasi-coherence hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Open-extension adjunction and exactness (00A7, 01AK); localization of a ringed-site morphism (04J0); derived functoriality (01F7), specialized to open-subscheme Ext adjunction and the cartesian scalar-extension square.

proof.text: Use the exact open-extension adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-zariski-extension-by-zero-adjunction, lem-weil-pbc-zariski-extension-by-zero-exact], transported between the localized open site and the opens of the open subscheme. The free sheaf L_W of [lem-pc-free-mayer-vietoris-short-exact] is j_! L_top(W), because both represent sections on W by the free/forgetful and sheafification adjunctions. Restriction identifies the underlying coefficient of j^*M with F|W. The Ext adjunction therefore gives t_n from Ext on W to Ext from L_W on X. Postcomposition naturality identifies restriction of each R-scalar and proves the first equation.

Let p:X_S→X and p_W:W_S→W be the projections defined in [def-pc-flat-cohomology-comparison]. The cartesian base-change square of j identifies W_S with the preimage open of W in X_S. Restriction commutes with direct image in this square (Stacks 04J0). Taking left adjoints identifies p^-1 j_! with j_S! p_W^-1, with the comparison determined by their units. Composition of module pullbacks identifies j_S^* p^*M with p_W^*j^*M. Applying the exact open-extension Ext adjunction on X_S gives t_n′. Naturality for S-scalar coefficient morphisms gives the second equation.

The units of the pullback/pushforward module adjunctions restrict to each other under the cartesian coefficient comparison. Their abelian adjoints, the displayed coefficient morphisms φ and φ_W of [def-pc-flat-cohomology-comparison], consequently commute with that comparison. Compute t_n and t_n′ by the Ext adjunction: apply exact extension by zero to an Ext class, then postcompose with the counit, and transport the representing free sheaf and coefficient isomorphisms. The base-change isomorphism of left adjoints intertwines their counits by uniqueness of mates. Functoriality of Ext under exact functors and associativity of Ext composition give the third equation. This is a statement entirely about Ext; no cohomology-to-Ext comparison is used. Empty opens and zero coefficients have zero Ext groups, and for the top open the constructions reduce to identity transport up to the canonical scheme isomorphisms.

theorem H.openFreeExtTransport (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of R)) (M : X.Modules) (W : X.Opens) :
    let F := (SheafOfModules.toSheaf X.ringCatSheaf).obj M
    let G := invImage (baseChangeFst (S := S) f)
    let N := (SheafOfModules.toSheaf (baseChangedScheme (S := S) f).ringCatSheaf).obj
      (baseChangedModule (S := S) f M)
    let φ := coeff (baseChangeFst (S := S) f) (baseChangeUnit (S := S) f M)
    let ρ := (scalarRep M).comp (((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of R)).inv ≫ f.appTop).hom)
    let τ := (scalarRep (baseChangedModule (S := S) f M)).comp
      (((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of S)).inv ≫ (baseChangeSnd (S := S) f).appTop).hom)
    let MW := (pullback W.ι).obj M
    let FW := (SheafOfModules.toSheaf W.toScheme.ringCatSheaf).obj MW
    let GW := invImage (baseChangeFst (S := S) (W.ι ≫ f))
    let NW := (SheafOfModules.toSheaf
      (baseChangedScheme (S := S) (W.ι ≫ f)).ringCatSheaf).obj
      (baseChangedModule (S := S) (W.ι ≫ f) MW)
    let φW := coeff (baseChangeFst (S := S) (W.ι ≫ f))
      (baseChangeUnit (S := S) (W.ι ≫ f) MW)
    let ρW := (scalarRep MW).comp
      (((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of R)).inv ≫ (W.ι ≫ f).appTop).hom)
    let τW := (scalarRep (baseChangedModule (S := S) (W.ι ≫ f) MW)).comp
      (((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of S)).inv ≫ (baseChangeSnd (S := S) (W.ι ≫ f)).appTop).hom)
    ∃ (t : ∀ n, Ext (H.openFreeSheaf (⊤ : W.toScheme.Opens)) FW n ≃+
        Ext (H.openFreeSheaf W) F n)
      (t' : ∀ n, Ext (GW.obj (H.openFreeSheaf (⊤ : W.toScheme.Opens))) NW n ≃+
        Ext (G.obj (H.openFreeSheaf W)) N n),
      (∀ n a x, t n (x.comp (Ext.mk₀ (ρW a)) (add_zero n)) =
        (t n x).comp (Ext.mk₀ (ρ a)) (add_zero n)) ∧
      (∀ n a x, t' n (x.comp (Ext.mk₀ (τW a)) (add_zero n)) =
        (t' n x).comp (Ext.mk₀ (τ a)) (add_zero n)) ∧
      (∀ n x, t' n ((x.mapExactFunctor GW).comp (Ext.mk₀ φW) (add_zero n)) =
        ((t n x).mapExactFunctor G).comp (Ext.mk₀ φ) (add_zero n))
